title: Extended Cech complex and Koszul dual limit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, and let $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ be global sections, allowing $r=0$. Use the module sheaves and their unbounded derived category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $P_m=\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{b_j^m}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $[0,r]$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with forward map $P_m\to P_{m+1}$ given in each factor by identity in degree zero and multiplication by $b_j$ in degree one. Equivalently the summand indexed by a subset $I$ in degree $|I|$ has transition multiplication by $\prod_{i\in I}b_i$. Its dual $Q_m=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m,\mathcal O)$, after the usual dual-complex sign identification, is the tensor of the factors $[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{b_j^m}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ with inverse maps $(b_j,1)$. Let $C_b$ be the extended alternating complex with degree-zero term $\mathcal O$, degree-$q$ term $\prod_{|I|=q}\mathcal O[1/\prod_{i\in I}b_i]$, alternating localization differential, and augmentation $\epsilon:C_b\to\mathcal O[0]$ equal to identity in degree zero. Localization means sheafified sectionwise localization. There is an augmentation-compatible identification $C_b\cong\operatorname{colim}_m P_m$, and this degreewise filtered colimit represents the homotopy colimit in $D(\mathcal O)$. For every $N\in D(\mathcal O)$, represented by a complex $N^\bullet$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\theta_N:R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(C_b,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim_m\operatorname{Tot}(N^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}Q_m).$$
Here derived internal Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; the tower on the right is a strict tower of complexes, each term represents $N\otimes^L Q_m$, and $R\lim$ is the total derived inverse limit computed with a K-injective strict-tower resolution, as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The isomorphism is independent of the representative of $N$ under the derived comparison maps. It carries $N\cong R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O,N)\xrightarrow{\epsilon^*}R\mathcal Hom(C_b,N)$ to the strict-tower unit induced by the degree-zero maps $\mathcal O\to Q_m$. For every object $U$, restriction of this comparison identifies its target with the corresponding strict derived limit on $\mathcal C/U$, and the comparisons commute with further slice restrictions and with morphisms in $N$. For the empty list $C_b=P_m=Q_m=\mathcal O[0]$ and the comparison and unit are the identity under the constant-tower identification.

proof.text: Expand $P_m$: its degree-$q$ summands have bases $e_I$ for $|I|=q$, and $d(e_I)=\sum_{j\notin I}(-1)^{|\{i\in I:i<j\}|}b_j^m e_{I\cup\{j\}}$. Put $t_I=\prod_{i\in I}b_i$. The identity $t_{I\cup\{j\}}b_j^m=t_I b_j^{m+1}$ verifies the forward maps are chain maps. Take $m\geq1$, equivalently stage $m-1$ of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. In the dual Hom differential, the one-factor differential is $b_j^m$ from degree $-1$ to degree $0$; the transition is $(b_j,1)$. For the multi-factor dual, evaluate $\phi_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\phi_r$ on $p_1\otimes\cdots\otimes p_r$ with sign $(-1)^{\sum_{a<b}|\phi_b||p_a|}$, moving each $\phi_b$ past the earlier $p_a$. Substitution into $d\phi=-(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi d_P$ gives the tensor dual differential, and degree-zero transition maps introduce no extra signs. Evaluation gives $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m,N)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes Q_m)$: on homogeneous $x\in N^a$, $\phi\in Q_m^c$, send $x\otimes\phi$ to $(p\mapsto\phi(p)x)$ for $p\in P_m^{-c}$. Inserting the Hom differential gives $d_Nx\otimes\phi+(-1)^a x\otimes d_Q\phi$, and precomposition by $P_m\to P_{m+1}$ becomes $1_N\otimes(Q_{m+1}\to Q_m)$.

proof.text: For $I$, send $a e_I$ at stage $m$ to $a/t_I^m$. This is compatible with transition multiplication by $t_I$. Every fraction is represented at a sufficiently large stage; $a/t_I^m=a'/t_I^{m'}$ means a power of $t_I$ kills the cross-multiplied difference, exactly equality at a later stage. Perform this calculation on sections and sheafify, as required for the colimit of module sheaves. The insertion term $b_j^m a e_{I\cup\{j\}}$ maps to $a/t_I^m$ localized at $b_j$, with the alternating sign from step 1. Thus both differentials and the degree-zero projection agree with $C_b$ and $\epsilon$. For $I=\varnothing$, $t_I=1$ and this is the constant copy of $\mathcal O$.

Every term of $P_m$ and $Q_m$ is a finite direct sum of $\mathcal O$. Such a term is flat: tensor with $\mathcal O^a$ is the finite direct-sum functor, hence preserves kernels and cokernels componentwise. Both complexes are bounded, so the bounded-above-flat theorem on sites makes them K-flat. In particular total tensor with $Q_m$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms: for a quasi-isomorphism $v$, its cone is acyclic, $\operatorname{Cone}(v)\otimes Q_m$ is acyclic by K-flatness, and the total-tensor differential identifies this with $\operatorname{Cone}(v\otimes1)$ (reorder the target and shifted-source summands; on the latter the differential is $-d_{source}+(-1)^p d_Q$ for original source degree $p+1$, exactly minus its total differential). The cone criterion proves the assertion. This applies to unbounded $N$.

Let $S=\bigoplus_m P_m$ and let $u:S\to S$ be identity minus the map sending the $m$-th summand to the $(m+1)$-st by its transition. The cited telescope theorem gives a canonical quasi-isomorphism $T=\operatorname{Cone}(u)\to C_b$. Hence $R\mathcal Hom(C_b,N)\to R\mathcal Hom(T,N)$ is an isomorphism. Choose the functorial K-injective resolution $N\to I$ supplied by the derived internal Hom definition, so the latter object is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(T,I)$.

Put $H_m=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m,I)=\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes Q_m)$ with the strict inverse transitions from step 1. Every $H_m$ is K-injective by the bounded split-projective tensor theorem (each term of $Q_m$ is finite free). Set $B=\prod_m H_m$ termwise. The product-K-injective theorem identifies $B$ with the product in $D(\mathcal O)$, without assuming exact products of sheaves. The sheaf Hom universal property gives $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(S,I)=B$; precomposition by $u$ is $1-s$, where $(s h)_m=h_{m+1}\circ(P_m\to P_{m+1})$. Expanding the two summands of the mapping cone and its Hom differential identifies $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(T,I)$ with the mapping fibre $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:B\to B)[-1]$, with differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-d_By-(1-s)x,d_Bx)$ in terms $B^{k-1}\oplus B^k$. Explicitly a degree-$k$ Hom element has components $(\alpha,\beta)$ on $S[1]$ and $S$; the identification is $(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto((-1)^{k-1}\alpha,\beta)$. Its differential becomes the displayed one by $d\alpha=d_B\alpha-(-1)^k u^*\beta$ and $d\beta=d_B\beta$.

proof.text: Write $H_\bullet=(\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m,I))_m$ and $B=\prod_m H_m$ as above. The small-diagram Grothendieck theorem, with index $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$, shows that $\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ is Grothendieck. Choose the functorial resolution $f:H_\bullet\to J_\bullet$ supplied by the degreewise-injective K-injective existence theorem. Thus $J_\bullet$ is K-injective as a tower complex and every $J^k$ is an injective tower. Evaluation is exact by the levelwise-abelian theorem, so $f_m:H_m\to J_m$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Evaluation preserves K-injectives, so each $J_m$ is K-injective. The strict-tower theorem identifies $R\lim H_\bullet$ with $\lim J_m$. No product-exactness hypothesis has been introduced.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), first and third paragraphs of the proof; injectives.tex Tag 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck).

proof.text: For a module $F$, let $L_m(F)$ be the tower with $F$ in levels $1,\ldots,m$, identity transitions there, and zero above $m$. A tower map $L_m(F)\to T$ is determined by its level-$m$ map $F\to T_m$, all lower components being its composites with transitions. Thus $L_m$ is left adjoint to evaluation. The natural inclusion $L_m(F)\hookrightarrow L_{m+1}(F)$ is componentwise monic. For the injective tower $J^k$, the injectivity extension property therefore makes $\operatorname{Hom}(F,J_{m+1}^k)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F,J_m^k)$ surjective. Taking $F=J_m^k$ gives a sheaf-module splitting $\sigma_m^k$ of each transition. Put $B_J=\prod_m J_m$. Given sections $y_m$ of $J_m^k$, set $x_1=0$ and $x_{m+1}=\sigma_m^k(x_m-y_m)$. Then $x_m-t_mx_{m+1}=y_m$. This is a sectionwise, restriction-compatible right inverse to $1-s_J$; each component uses only finitely many operations. Its kernel is $\lim J_m$ by the limit universal property. Apply the degreewise-epimorphism kernel-to-fibre lemma to obtain the canonical quasi-isomorphism $\kappa_J:\lim J_m\to F_J=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_J:B_J\to B_J)[-1]$, $z\mapsto(0,z)$.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), injective transitions and final short exact sequence; explicit module-sheaf splitting argument.

proof.text: Since $H_m$ and $J_m$ are K-injective, the comparison principle makes every $f_m$ a homotopy equivalence. Indeed it supplies $g_m$ with $g_m f_m\simeq1$; injectivity of precomposition by $f_m$ into the K-injective target $J_m$ then gives $f_m g_m\simeq1$. Taking products of these inverses and homotopies makes $b=\prod f_m:B\to B_J$ a homotopy equivalence. The map $b$ strictly commutes with $1-s$ because $f$ is a tower map. Hence it induces the diagonal chain map $F(f):F_H=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:B\to B)[-1]\to F_J$. The two copies of $b$ and this cone map form a morphism of cone triangles. The triangle isomorphism lemma shows $F(f)$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O)$. Therefore $F_H\xrightarrow{F(f)}F_J\xleftarrow{\kappa_J}\lim J_m$ canonically identifies $F_H$ with $R\lim H_\bullet$. Naturality holds because $J$, $f$, $\kappa_J$, and the diagonal fibre map are functorial; the component homotopy inverses were used only to prove that this specified map is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), comparing the strict resolution with the termwise K-injective Roos model; derived.tex Tag 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle).

proof.text: Use the K-flatness established in step 3 with the functorial resolution $N^\bullet\to I$. It gives a levelwise quasi-isomorphism of strict towers $T(N)_m=\operatorname{Tot}(N^\bullet\otimes Q_m)\to H_m=\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes Q_m)$. Exactness and cohomology in towers are levelwise, so this map is a quasi-isomorphism in the tower category. It becomes invertible in its derived category, and applying the total derived inverse-limit functor gives an isomorphism $R\lim T(N)\to R\lim H$. Define $\theta_N$ by composing the isomorphisms of steps 4--5 and 8 with the inverse of this last map. A quasi-isomorphism $N^\bullet\to(N')^\bullet$ gives the same commuting diagram, by the tensor and Hom evaluation of step 1 and the functorial resolution. Both constructions invert all quasi-isomorphisms, so localization gives a natural isomorphism on $D(\mathcal O)$, independent of representatives under their derived comparison maps.

proof.text: The projections $P_m\to\mathcal O[0]$ give $T\to C_b\xrightarrow{\epsilon}\mathcal O[0]$ of step 4. For $x\in I^k$, precomposition sends $x$ to the family of degree-$k$ Hom maps supported on $P_m^0$, with value $x$ there. Step 1 identifies these with the degree-zero inclusions $I\to I\otimes Q_m$. The map on the shifted summand of the telescope is zero. Thus its fibre coordinates are exactly $(0,(x)_m)$. After $F(f)$ this is $(0,(f_m(x))_m)=\kappa_J((f_m(x))_m)$, where the compatible family is the factorization $I\to\lim J_m$ of the unit maps. Consequently $\kappa_J^{-1}F(f)$ carries the augmentation map to the ordinary-limit unit followed by its derived comparison. Naturality of that comparison for $N^\bullet\to I$, and then inversion of $R\lim T(N)\to R\lim H$, proves the stated equality for $\theta_N$.

source.place: Tag 0A0A (lemma-colim-and-lim-of-duals), explicit augmentation and degree-zero unit in the Koszul specialization.

proof.text: Restriction to $\mathcal C/U$ is exact, and $I|_U$ is K-injective by the restriction lemma. The Hom-complex definition, evaluated over every $V\to U$, gives $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I)|_U=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L|_U,I|_U)$. Products are sectionwise, so restriction preserves $B$, $1-s$, and the finite-sum cone $F_H$. Restricting finite free tensor factors gives the same ordered tensor factors and evaluation maps over $\mathcal O|_U$. Thus the isomorphism from $R\mathcal Hom(C_b,N)|_U$ to $F_H|_U$ is precisely the one constructed on the slice. The derived internal-Hom restriction theorem identifies its source with $R\mathcal Hom(C_b|_U,N|_U)$. Steps 6--9 on the slice identify its target fibre with the strict derived limit there, yielding the asserted target restriction identification. On an object $W\to V\to U$, every component is the restriction of the same evaluation, transition, and projection map; hence these comparisons and the map $(0,(x)_m)$ of step 10 commute with further restriction. The same formulas commute with morphisms in $N$. This establishes the comparison for these towers without asserting exactness of products of sheaves.

source.place: Tag 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U); label lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok) on the slice.

proof.text: For $r=0$, the empty tensors are $P_m=Q_m=\mathcal O[0]$, all transitions are identities, and $C_b=\mathcal O[0]$. In the fibre model $B=\prod_m I$ the chain map $1-s$ is split surjective: $y\mapsto x$ with $x_1=0$ and $x_{m+1}=x_m-y_m$ is a chain-map right inverse, since each component is a finite sum. Its kernel is the diagonal copy of $I$. The kernel-to-fibre lemma identifies $I$ with $F_H$ by $x\mapsto(0,(x)_m)$. This is exactly the map of step 10; therefore $\theta_N$ and the unit are the identity under the constant-tower identification. The same calculation also covers the zero coefficient sheaf. No nonzero or regularity hypothesis on the list was used anywhere.
